title: Nifty holds flat at open despite Wall Street gains; FII selling streak hits 11 sessions - The HinduBusinessLine
text:
FILE PHOTO: Monday’s flat open follows the indices snapping an eight-week losing streak last week, with the Nifty gaining 0.44% and Sensex advancing 562 points over the five-day period. | Photo Credit: FRANCIS MASCARENHAS

Equity benchmarks opened on a cautious note on Monday with the Nifty 50 opening at 22,593.20 against a previous close of 22,520.45, and trading near 22,525.60, up just 5.15 points or 0.02 per cent, at 9.25 am. The Sensex opened at 72,771.32 compared to its previous close of 72,472.33, before slipping to 72,426.28, down 46.05 points or 0.06 per cent, at the same time. The flat open follows the indices snapping an eight-week losing streak last week, with the Nifty gaining 0.44 per cent and the Sensex advancing 562 points over the five-day period.

Among the top gainers on the Nifty 50, Bajaj Auto led with its stock at ₹10,073, up 3.02 per cent from a previous close of ₹9,778. BSE gained 1.64 per cent to ₹3,341 from ₹3,287.20. Mahindra & Mahindra rose 1.31 per cent to ₹2,832.90 from ₹2,796.20. Bharat Electronics added 1.17 per cent to ₹372.45 from ₹368.15, while Dr. Reddy’s Laboratories climbed 1.08 per cent to ₹1,209.90 from ₹1,197.

On the losing side, Tech Mahindra was the steepest faller, down 4.24 per cent to ₹1,449.90 from ₹1,514.10. ITC declined 1 per cent to ₹263.35 from ₹266. Axis Bank shed 0.95 per cent to ₹1,247.20 from ₹1,259.10. Bharti Airtel fell 0.73 per cent to ₹1,792 from ₹1,805.10, and State Bank of India slipped 0.56 per cent to ₹953.70 from ₹959.10.

Foreign institutional investors extended their selling streak to 11 consecutive sessions on October 9, recording net sales of ₹3,568 crore. Weekly FII outflows stood at ₹35,556 crore. Domestic institutional investors continued to absorb the selling pressure with net purchases of approximately ₹4,743 crore on Friday.

“The market is going through a stage wherein external headwinds are dominating domestic tailwinds,” said Dr. V K Vijayakumar, Chief Investment Strategist at Geojit Investments Ltd. “Elevated crude prices and high US bond yields will continue to impact the market. FIIs will continue to sell in the near-term and DIIs will continue to absorb the FII selling.”

Brent crude traded near $103–104 a barrel, while the rupee remained under pressure at ₹96.73 against the US dollar. Over the weekend, the Reserve Bank of India established a direct dollar-supply window for state-run oil companies and raised the minimum daily Cash Reserve Ratio maintenance requirement for scheduled banks from 90 per cent to 99 per cent, steps aimed at easing currency depreciation pressure. “These emergency steps immediately remove massive daily oil-import demand from the open spot market and squeeze out speculators,” noted Devarsh Vakil, Head of Prime Research at HDFC Securities.

“Indian equities are likely to open on a positive note, with GIFT Nifty at 22,635, up 32 points,” said Deepesh Sarawagi, Technical Research Analyst at Choice Broking. “Investors will also track the RBI’s latest measures to support the rupee, along with upcoming Indian and US inflation data and corporate earnings this week.”

In sectoral terms, IT led Friday’s recovery alongside Auto, Metal, Media, FMCG and Pharma. Over the previous week, Capital Markets and FMCG outperformed with gains of nearly 2.5 per cent each. Realty and Metal remained under pressure, falling more than 3.5 per cent. BSE Midcap and Smallcap indices lost 0.5 per cent and 0.4 per cent week-on-week, respectively.

US markets closed higher on Friday, with the Dow Jones rising 0.8 per cent and both the S&P 500 and Nasdaq gaining 0.6 per cent. Asian markets were mixed Monday, with South Korea’s KOSPI falling more than 1 per cent and Japan’s Nikkei 225 closed for a holiday. The US 10-year Treasury yield stood near 5.24 per cent, close to a 24-year peak.

India’s year-to-date return stood at -13.87 per cent, making it one of the worst-performing markets globally. “For investors with a medium-to-long-term investment horizon, this market provides value buying opportunities,” Vijayakumar said. “If crude declines sharply following favourable developments in West Asia, the market can rally significantly from the current levels. Patience is the key.”
